title: Create True-Shape Links
text:
2 Load Data

Candidate Centerlines
CandidateTDMRoadLinks.gpkg (built in 00_data_preparation.qmd) is already filtered and dissolved, but it is also pre-cut at arcpy-style junction points — including incidental boundaries between freeway/ramp/CD rows and surface-street rows wherever they merely touch, not just at genuine multi-way branches. Part A below re-dissolves these rows into maximal chains so that every split point in the final pieces (Part C) comes only from snapping, not from CandidateTDMRoadLinks’s own pre-existing cuts.


Show the code
gdf_centerlines = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_centerlines"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)

print(f"Candidate components: {len(gdf_centerlines):,} | CRS: {gdf_centerlines.crs}")


Candidate components: 7,642 | CRS: EPSG:26912




Snapped Nodes


Show the code
gdf_nodes_snapped = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_cc_snapped    = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="cc_nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_ext_snapped   = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="ext_nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)

n_total   = len(gdf_nodes_snapped)
n_snapped = gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"].fillna(False).sum()
print(f"Nodes: {n_total:,} total | {n_snapped:,} snapped ({n_snapped/n_total:.1%})")
print(f"CC attachment nodes: {len(gdf_cc_snapped):,}")
print(f"External station nodes: {len(gdf_ext_snapped):,}")


Nodes: 21,953 total | 3,546 snapped (16.2%)
CC attachment nodes: 6,539
External station nodes: 29




Show the code
gdf_nodes_snapped[gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"]].explore()

title: Create True-Shape Links
text:
3 Part A — Resolve Snap Coordinates
nodes_snapped.gpkg stores snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round rounded to 2 decimal places (cm precision). Splitting and M-value operations require coordinates that exactly match a vertex stored in the centerline geometry. For each snapped node, this step finds the nearest unique centerline vertex within 5 cm and records its full-precision coordinate.
FixedTransit_Rail nodes are excluded — they snap to GTFS rail infrastructure (CRT stations, LRT midpoints), not to road centerlines, so they are never road centerline split points.


Show the code
gdf_nodes_road = gdf_nodes_snapped[
    gdf_nodes_snapped["snap_rule"] != "FixedTransit_Rail"
]
gdf_nodes_resolved = resolve_snap_coords(
    gdf_nodes_road,
    gdf_centerlines,
    tolerance=0.05,
)

n_road_snapped = gdf_nodes_road["snapped"].fillna(False).sum()
n_resolved     = gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"].sum()
n_unresolved   = n_road_snapped - n_resolved
print(f"Coordinate resolution: {n_resolved:,} resolved | {n_unresolved:,} unresolved")


Coordinate resolution: 3,600 resolved | 0 unresolved




Show the code
if n_unresolved > 0:
    unresolved = gdf_nodes_resolved[
        gdf_nodes_resolved["snapped"].fillna(False) & ~gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"]
    ]
    print("Unresolved node sample (check snap quality):")
    print(unresolved[["N", "snap_rule", "snapped_x_round", "snapped_y_round"]].head(10).to_string())


Build the list of exact-coordinate Points used as split locations.


Show the code
resolved_mask = gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"]
snap_points_exact = [
    Point(row["x_exact"], row["y_exact"])
    for _, row in gdf_nodes_resolved[resolved_mask].iterrows()
]
print(f"Split points prepared: {len(snap_points_exact):,}")


Split points prepared: 3,600

title: Create True-Shape Links
text:
4 Part B — Merge Centerlines
Fuse consecutive segments at degree-2 vertices via linemerge. Real intersections (3+ roads meeting) remain as line endpoints and are not merged.


Show the code
print("Merging centerlines …")
cl_merged = merge_centerlines(gdf_centerlines)

if cl_merged.geom_type == "MultiLineString":
    n_components = len(cl_merged.geoms)
elif cl_merged.geom_type == "LineString":
    n_components = 1
else:
    n_components = sum(1 for g in cl_merged.geoms if g.geom_type == "LineString")

total_length_km = sum(
    g.length for g in (cl_merged.geoms if hasattr(cl_merged, "geoms") else [cl_merged])
) / 1000
print(f"Merged: {n_components:,} components | total length: {total_length_km:,.1f} km")


Merging centerlines …
Merged: 6,917 components | total length: 5,945.9 km

title: Create True-Shape Links
section: 6 Part C — Split at Snapped Nodes
text:
6 Part C — Split at Snapped Nodes
gdf_fulldissolve_restitched (Part A + B2) — not the original CandidateTDMRoadLinks rows — is split only at snapped road model-node positions, so piece boundaries come exclusively from road-node snapping, never from incidental arcpy junction cuts or an incidental same-route junction (VERT_LEVEL boundary or unrelated at-grade crossing). Points that project to within 0.1 mm of a component’s existing endpoint are skipped (already a boundary). After all splits, each resulting piece is bounded exclusively by: - a snapped model node position, or - a genuine branch/route-identity-mismatch junction already present in gdf_fulldissolve_restitched.
CC attachment nodes (cc_nodes_snapped) and external station nodes (ext_nodes_snapped) are also used as split points here, but only the use_as_split subset — resolved within 100 m and not already snapped by the main pipeline (see Part B and 01_node_classification.qmd). Unresolved nodes are left out entirely, same as any other unsnapped node: no coordinate, no split, no change from today’s behavior for that node.
No lineage keys are carried through this split (id_cols=()) — a redissolved row no longer maps 1:1 to a single original OBJECTID. Lineage/display attributes are reattached afterward via midpoint join (Part D).


Show the code
all_snap_points = snap_points_exact + cc_points_exact + ext_points_exact
print(
    f"Split points: {len(snap_points_exact):,} model nodes "
    f"+ {len(cc_points_exact):,} CC attachment "
    f"+ {len(ext_points_exact):,} external station "
    f"= {len(all_snap_points):,} total"
)


Split points: 3,476 model nodes + 4,578 CC attachment + 14 external station = 8,068 total




Show the code
print(f"Splitting {len(gdf_fulldissolve_restitched):,} redissolved chains at {len(all_snap_points):,} points …")
gdf_pieces_split = split_candidate_links(gdf_fulldissolve_restitched, all_snap_points, id_cols=())
print(f"Pieces after split: {len(gdf_pieces_split):,}")


Splitting 6,160 redissolved chains at 8,068 points …
Pieces after split: 11,200

title: Create True-Shape Links
section: 6 Part D — Build Pieces Layer and Export
text:
6 Part D — Build Pieces Layer and Export
Extract start/end endpoint coordinates for each piece (rounded to 2 dp for matching against snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round in the next stage), then export as link_pieces.gpkg with the inherited lineage-key columns.


Show the code
pieces = gdf_pieces_split.geometry.tolist()
start_coords = np.array([p.coords[0] for p in pieces])
end_coords   = np.array([p.coords[-1] for p in pieces])

gdf_pieces = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "piece_id": np.arange(len(pieces)),
        "x_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "x_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "length_m": np.array([p.length for p in pieces]),
        "geometry": pieces,
    },
    crs=CRS_UTM,
)

PATHS["out_link_pieces"].parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gdf_pieces.to_file(PATHS["out_link_pieces"], driver="GPKG")
print(f"Exported {len(gdf_pieces):,} pieces → {PATHS['out_link_pieces']}")


Exported 12,252 pieces → _data\processed\link_pieces.gpkg

text:
2 Load Data

Roadway Centerlines


Show the code
# Cleaned and attributed centerlines produced by 00_data_preparation.qmd.
# Retired/Planned segments and DupRoute aliases are already excluded.
# Whitespace in DOT_FCLASS and CARTOCODE is already stripped.
gdf_centerlines = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_centerlines"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)
print(f"Centerlines: {len(gdf_centerlines):,} features | CRS: {gdf_centerlines.crs}")


Centerlines: 7,642 features | CRS: EPSG:26912




Show the code
gdf_centerlines.head(1000).explore()




Network Links and Nodes


Show the code
# Active 2027 links, excluding HOV / Managed Lane / Managed Lane Access (FT 37-39).
# These are filtered at load time so they never inflate LinkCount, contribute to
# the direction cascade, or generate spurious "surface" node classifications.
gdf_links = gpd.read_file(
    PATHS["in_network_links"],
    where="LN_2027 > 0 AND FT_2027 NOT IN (1, 37, 38, 39)",
).to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_nodes = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_network_nodes"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)

print(f"Links: {len(gdf_links):,} (LN_2027 > 0, FT not in 1/37/38/39)")

Links: 28,101 (LN_2027 > 0, FT not in 1/37/38/39)
Nodes: 21,953




Show the code
gdf_links.head(1000).explore()
gdf_nodes.head(1000).explore()




GTFS Rail Stops
Filter GTFS stops to Light Rail (TRAX, route_type 0) and Commuter Rail (FrontRunner, route_type 2) only, walking the routes → trips → stop_times chain.


Show the code
feed = gk.read_feed(PATHS["in_gtfs"], dist_units="km")

gdf_stops  = gk.get_stops(feed,  as_gdf=True).to_crs(PROJ_UTM12N)
gdf_shapes = gk.get_shapes(feed, as_gdf=True).to_crs(PROJ_UTM12N)
gdf_routes = gk.get_routes(feed, as_gdf=True).to_crs(PROJ_UTM12N)

RAIL_ROUTE_TYPES = {0, 2}   # 0 = Light Rail (TRAX), 2 = Commuter Rail (FrontRunner)

rail_route_ids = feed.routes.loc[feed.routes["route_type"].isin(RAIL_ROUTE_TYPES), "route_id"]
rail_trip_ids  = feed.trips.loc[feed.trips["route_id"].isin(rail_route_ids), "trip_id"]
rail_stop_ids  = feed.stop_times.loc[feed.stop_times["trip_id"].isin(rail_trip_ids), "stop_id"].unique()

gdf_rail_stops = gdf_stops[gdf_stops["stop_id"].isin(rail_stop_ids)].copy()
print(f"Rail stops: {len(gdf_rail_stops):,} of {len(gdf_stops):,} total stops")

gdf_rail_stops.explore()

title: Node Classification
text:
3 Part A — Origin Processing (Network Nodes)

A1 — Functional Type Flags
nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links, ft_codes) returns True for any node whose N appears as endpoint A or B of at least one link whose FT code is in ft_codes.
Flags are non-exclusive — a node touching both a freeway and a ramp link will be True for both Freeway and Ramp. Mutual exclusion is enforced later in the topology cascade (§A3).


Show the code
# ── Three mutually exclusive TDM link classes (2027 network year) ─────────
#
# FT_2027 code reference
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Class 1 — Freeway Mainline (FW_CODES):
#   12-15  Expressway (limited-access, divided)
#   22-26  MM freeway (posted 55-75 mph, MM series)
#   32-36  Freeway    (posted 55-75 mph, Fwy series)
#   40     Express / managed-access freeway
#   FT=2 AND DIRECTION=1: directional Principal Arterial links representing
#         physically separated roadways (e.g. divided expressways coded as PA).
#
# Class 2 — Ramps and CDs (RAMP_CODES):
#   20/30  Loop ramps  |  28/29  MM on/off ramps  |  41/42  Fwy on/off ramps
#   21/31  CD roads (collector-distributor geometry)
#
# Class 3 — Surface Streets (SURFACE_CODES):
#   2/3  Principal/Minor Arterial  |  4/5  Major/Minor Collector  |  6/7  Local/Unpaved
#   FT=2 links with DIRECTION=1 are excluded (they belong to Class 1 above).
#
# Filtered out at load time (not present in gdf_links):
#   1  Centroid connector (zone-to-network tap, not a physical road)
#   37 HOV lane  |  38 Managed lane  |  39 Managed-lane access point
#   Removed before any processing so they cannot inflate LinkCount/NeighborCount,
#   corrupt the pseudonode LinkClassCount check, pollute the direction cascade,
#   or produce spurious surface-type node classifications.
#
# Loaded but excluded from the three road classes:
#   70/80 Fixed transit  |  N ranges 10000-19999 and 50000-59999 (station nodes)
#   Transit geometry is handled separately in the FixedTransit snapping pass.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

FT_COL = "FT_2027"

# DIRECTION=1 flag: handles both numeric 1 and string "1" encodings
_oneway = gdf_links["ONEWAY"].astype(str).str.strip() == "1"

# Mutually exclusive link masks (LN_2027 > 0 already filtered at load time)

# 1. Freeway includes interstates and expressways/principal arterials that have directional travel
FWY_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 40}) | (
    gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({2, 12, 13, 14, 15}) & _oneway
)

# 2. Ramp and Collector-Distributor Roads share the same mask
RAMP_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({20, 21, 28, 29, 30, 31, 41, 42})

# 3. Centroid Connectors (FT = 1)
CC_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL] == 1

# 4. HOV and Managed Lanes (FT = 37, 38, 39)
MANAGED_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({37, 38, 39})

# 5. Remaining Links get assigned as Surface Links
SURFACE_LINK_MASK = ~(FWY_LINK_MASK | RAMP_LINK_MASK | CC_LINK_MASK | MANAGED_LINK_MASK)

# FW_CODES: FT codes used for the freeway-priority direction cascade.
# FT=2+DIRECTION=1 is classified as freeway but excluded here because its
# DIRECTION value is a one-way flag, not a cardinal (NB/SB/EB/WB).
# Direction matching for those links is deferred to the geometric heading
# approach planned for the ramp refactor (Request 3).
FW_CODES = {12, 13, 14, 15, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 40}

gdf_nodes["Freeway"] = nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links[FWY_LINK_MASK])
gdf_nodes["Ramp"] = nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links[RAMP_LINK_MASK])
gdf_nodes["Surface"] = nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links[SURFACE_LINK_MASK])
gdf_nodes["FixedTransit"] = (
    nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links, {70, 80})
    | gdf_nodes["N"].between(10_000, 19_999)  # TRAX station nodes
    | gdf_nodes["N"].between(50_000, 59_999)  # FrontRunner station nodes
)

flag_cols = ["Freeway", "Ramp", "Surface", "FixedTransit"]
print("Flag counts:")
print(gdf_nodes[flag_cols].sum().rename("NodeCount").to_frame().to_string())
print(
    f"\nLinks by class — Freeway: {FWY_LINK_MASK.sum():,}  "
    f"| Ramp: {RAMP_LINK_MASK.sum():,}  "
    f"| Surface: {SURFACE_LINK_MASK.sum():,}"
)


Flag counts:
              NodeCount
Freeway            1890
Ramp               1629
Surface           10795
FixedTransit        616

Links by class — Freeway: 1,874  | Ramp: 1,341  | Surface: 24,886




A2 — Link Count, Neighbor Count, and Direction
count_links adds LinkCount — raw endpoint references per node, used for the distribution chart and diagnostics.
count_neighbors adds NeighborCount — the number of distinct neighboring nodes. This is the topologically correct pseudonode test: LinkCount breaks on bidirectional roads stored as two directional records (a pseudonode appears 4 times → LinkCount=4, not 2), while NeighborCount is always 2 for a true shape vertex regardless of storage convention.
A node is an is_pseudo shape vertex if and only if all three conditions hold: 1. NeighborCount == 2 — lies on a single path between two real junctions. 2. LinkFTCount == 1 — all connected links share the same exact FT code. A node where FT changes (e.g. FT 32→33) has a real physical endpoint in the centerline data and must be sent to snapping. 3. LinkLNCount == 1 — all connected links carry the same lane count. A lane-drop or lane-add node must not be dissolved away, as doing so would erase a model attribute boundary that affects TDM impedance.
assign_node_directions produces two direction columns (see docstring): - link_directions — freeway-priority cascade; used in passes (a) and (c). - fw_directions — freeway links only, majority-vote; used in pass (b) gore nodes.


Show the code
gdf_nodes = count_links(gdf_nodes, gdf_links)
gdf_nodes = count_neighbors(gdf_nodes, gdf_links)
gdf_nodes = assign_node_directions(gdf_nodes, gdf_links, freeway_ft_codes=FW_CODES)

# Assign one class label per link using the already-defined mutually exclusive masks.
_link_class = pd.Series("other", index=gdf_links.index)
_link_class[FWY_LINK_MASK]  = "freeway"
_link_class[RAMP_LINK_MASK] = "ramp"
_link_class[SURFACE_LINK_MASK] = "surface"
_link_class[gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({70, 80})] = "transit"

# For each node, count how many distinct link classes touch it.
_stacked_class = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A"]].assign(cls=_link_class.values).rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B"]].assign(cls=_link_class.values).rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
_class_counts = _stacked_class.groupby("N")["cls"].nunique()
gdf_nodes["LinkClassCount"] = gdf_nodes["N"].map(_class_counts).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Count distinct FT codes per node.
# Stricter than LinkClassCount: nodes where FT changes (e.g. FT=32→33) register
# LinkFTCount=2 even though both belong to the freeway class.  Used in the
# link true-shape dissolution step to preserve model link boundaries where posted
# speed or facility sub-type changes — dissolving those nodes would corrupt TDM impedance.
_stacked_ft = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A", FT_COL]].rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B", FT_COL]].rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
_ft_counts = _stacked_ft.groupby("N")[FT_COL].nunique()
gdf_nodes["LinkFTCount"] = gdf_nodes["N"].map(_ft_counts).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Count distinct lane counts per node — lane-drop/lane-add nodes must be snapped
# even when FT is uniform, because dissolving them would erase the lane change.
_stacked_ln = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A", "LN_2027"]].rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B", "LN_2027"]].rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
_ln_counts = _stacked_ln.groupby("N")["LN_2027"].nunique()
gdf_nodes["LinkLNCount"] = gdf_nodes["N"].map(_ln_counts).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Pseudonode: shape vertex on a single homogeneous path — no physical snap target.
# Requires uniform FT AND uniform lane count: a lane-drop node has a real physical
# endpoint in the centerline data and must not be dissolved away. is_pseudo gates
# Part A3's node_type assignment below (a pseudonode gets no node_type / is never
# sent to spatial snapping) and must stay this strict — a snapping target still
# needs FT/LN uniformity to be a safe physical match.
gdf_nodes["is_pseudo"] = (
    (gdf_nodes["NeighborCount"] == 2)
    & (gdf_nodes["LinkFTCount"] == 1)
    & (gdf_nodes["LinkLNCount"] == 1)
)

# Broader topological pass-through flag, for Stage 3 chain dissolution only
# (03_transfer_attributes.qmd) — NOT used for snapping eligibility here.
# NeighborCount==2 alone is a sufficient safety guarantee on its own: a node
# with exactly two distinct neighbors has exactly one way to walk through it,
# regardless of whether FT, lane count, or link class (freeway/ramp/surface
# designation) changes there. Dropping the uniform-FT/uniform-LN/uniform-class
# requirements here (unlike is_pseudo above) lets Stage 3 dissolve through
# real FT/lane-transition and class-transition nodes that have no physical
# vertex of their own — the dominant cause of `endpoints_only` pieces, see
# _plan/freeway-endpoint-pool-diagnosis.md and the node-30208 (Antelope Island
# Causeway) example that first surfaced it. A node with 3+ neighbors is never
# included regardless — with a real branch, topology alone can't tell you
# which branch continues the same physical road (see dissolve_pseudonodes'
# docstring), so it must stay a hard boundary.
gdf_nodes["is_topo_passthrough"] = gdf_nodes["NeighborCount"] == 2

print(f"Pseudonodes (NeighborCount==2, uniform FT+LN): {gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'].sum():,}")
print(f"  of which LinkCount==2: {(gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'] & (gdf_nodes['LinkCount'] == 2)).sum():,}")
print(f"  of which LinkCount> 2: {(gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'] & (gdf_nodes['LinkCount'] > 2)).sum():,}  ← bidirectional road pseudonodes")
print(f"Class-transition nodes (NeighborCount==2, multi-class): {((gdf_nodes['NeighborCount'] == 2) & (gdf_nodes['LinkClassCount'] > 1)).sum():,}  ← real junctions, must be snapped")
print(f"FT-transition nodes sent to snapping (NeighborCount==2, same class, diff FT): {((gdf_nodes['NeighborCount'] == 2) & (gdf_nodes['LinkClassCount'] == 1) & (gdf_nodes['LinkFTCount'] > 1)).sum():,}")
print(f"LN-transition nodes sent to snapping (NeighborCount==2, uniform FT, diff LN): {((gdf_nodes['NeighborCount'] == 2) & (gdf_nodes['LinkFTCount'] == 1) & (gdf_nodes['LinkLNCount'] > 1)).sum():,}")
print(f"is_topo_passthrough (NeighborCount==2, any FT/LN/class): {gdf_nodes['is_topo_passthrough'].sum():,}  ← Stage 3 dissolve set (broader than is_pseudo by {gdf_nodes['is_topo_passthrough'].sum() - gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'].sum():,})")


Pseudonodes (NeighborCount==2, uniform FT+LN): 8,885
  of which LinkCount==2: 1,508
  of which LinkCount> 2: 7,377  ← bidirectional road pseudonodes
Class-transition nodes (NeighborCount==2, multi-class): 23  ← real junctions, must be snapped
FT-transition nodes sent to snapping (NeighborCount==2, same class, diff FT): 130
LN-transition nodes sent to snapping (NeighborCount==2, uniform FT, diff LN): 133
is_topo_passthrough (NeighborCount==2, any FT/LN/class): 9,167  ← Stage 3 dissolve set (broader than is_pseudo by 282)




Show the code
# Link-count distribution chart
link_count_freq = gdf_nodes["LinkCount"].value_counts().sort_index()
max_val = link_count_freq.max()

BASE_COLOR   = "#B4B2A9"
ACCENT_COLOR = "#1D9E75"
PSEUDO_COLOR = "#EF9F27"

bar_colors = [
    PSEUDO_COLOR if lc == 2 else (ACCENT_COLOR if lc in {4, 6, 8} else BASE_COLOR)
    for lc in link_count_freq.index
]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.5))
fig.patch.set_facecolor("white")
ax.set_facecolor("white")
ax.yaxis.grid(True, color=GRID_COLOR, linewidth=0.6, zorder=0)

for bar in bars:
    h = bar.get_height()
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, h + max_val * 0.012,
            f"{int(h):,}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5, color=LABEL_COLOR)

for spine in ["top", "right", "left"]:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(GRID_COLOR)
ax.set_xticks(link_count_freq.index)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f"{int(x):,}"))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=9.5, colors="#888780", length=0)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0)

ax.set_xlabel("Number of links connected to node", fontsize=10.5, color="#888780", labelpad=10)

ax.legend(
    [plt.Rectangle((0,0),1,1,color=c) for c in [ACCENT_COLOR, PSEUDO_COLOR, BASE_COLOR]],
    ["Typical intersection (4, 6, 8)", "Pseudonode (2)", "Other"],
    loc="upper right", fontsize=9, frameon=False, labelcolor="#888780",
)
fig.text(0.13, 1.01, "Most nodes connect to 4, 6, or 8 links",
         fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", color=LABEL_COLOR, transform=ax.transAxes)
fig.text(0.13, 0.94, f"Distribution of {len(gdf_nodes):,} network nodes by link count",
         fontsize=10.5, color="#888780", transform=ax.transAxes)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()











A3 — Node Topology Classification
Eight mutually-exclusive node_type labels. Transit is evaluated first and takes priority over all road-class combinations. The remaining seven labels derive from the full combinatorics of the (Freeway, Ramp, Surface) flags.
HOV/managed-lane nodes (FT 37-39) were filtered at load time, so they contribute no flags; those nodes fall to “surface” and are not snapped. Pseudonodes (LinkCount == 2) are shape vertices with no physical counterpart.


Show the code
no_pseudo = ~gdf_nodes["is_pseudo"]

is_fwy_node     = gdf_nodes["Freeway"]      & no_pseudo
is_ramp_node    = gdf_nodes["Ramp"]         & no_pseudo
is_surface_node = gdf_nodes["Surface"]      & no_pseudo
is_transit_node = gdf_nodes["FixedTransit"] & no_pseudo

# Full combinatorics of the three link classes → 7 node types.
# Transit is evaluated first — station nodes get "transit" regardless of any
# road-class links they may also touch.
# Most-specific road combinations (all three flags) are evaluated next.
gdf_nodes["node_type"] = np.select(
    [
        is_transit_node,                                  # fixed rail station
        is_fwy_node &  is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node,  # fwy+ramp+sf → at-grade interchange
        is_fwy_node &  is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node,  # fwy+ramp    → elevated gore
        is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node,  # fwy+sf      → at-grade fwy crossing
        is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node,  # fwy only    → pure mainline
        ~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node,  # ramp+sf     → ramp terminal
        ~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node,  # ramp only   → mid-ramp
    ],
    ["transit", "gore_sf", "gore", "fwy_sf", "fwy", "ramp_sf", "ramp"],
    default="surface",
)

print("Node type distribution:")
print(gdf_nodes["node_type"].value_counts().rename("count").to_frame().to_string())

title: Node Classification
text:
4 Part B — Target Processing (Centerline Endpoints)
The endpoint layer makes topology and direction assignments explicit and inspectable in QGIS before any snapping happens. The full workflow is: B1 filter to active segments → B2 classify segments → B3 extract endpoints → B4 deduplicate → B5 assign directions → B6 assign ep_type → B7 export.

B1 — Filter to Active Segments


Show the code
# Retired/Planned segments and DupRoute aliases were excluded at data-prep time.
# CARTOCODE '99' marks features excluded from standard cartographic display
# (tunnels, grade-separated service roads) — exclude from snapping pools.
_cartocode_ok = gdf_centerlines["CARTOCODE"].fillna("") != "99"

# Ramp/CD segments may have blank DOT_FCLASS but a valid DOT_RTNAME — keep them.
_is_ramp_seg = (
    gdf_centerlines["DOT_RTNAME"].fillna("").str.contains("R", na=False)
    | gdf_centerlines["DOT_RTNAME"].fillna("").str.contains("C", na=False)
)
_fclass_ok = (
    gdf_centerlines["DOT_FCLASS"].notna()
    & ~gdf_centerlines["DOT_FCLASS"].isin(["Instituitional", ""])
)

active_cl = gdf_centerlines[_cartocode_ok & (_fclass_ok | _is_ramp_seg)].copy()
print(f"Active centerlines: {len(active_cl):,} of {len(gdf_centerlines):,}")


Active centerlines: 7,642 of 7,642




B2 — Classify Segments
Three mutually exclusive boolean flags per segment. Primary authority is DOT_FCLASS for freeway identification; DOT_RTNAME (UDOT LRS) supplements with explicit route numbers and ramp/CD facility characters. ONEWAY in (1, 2) elevates divided Principal Arterials into the freeway class (domain CVDomain_OneWay: 0=Two-way, 1=One-way direction of arc, 2=One-way opposite direction of arc).
DOT_RTNAME layout (11 characters, zero-padded):
  [0:4]  Route number      e.g. "0015" = I-15, "0154" = Bangerter
  [4]    LRS direction     "P" = primary (NB/EB),  "N" = negative (SB/WB)
  [5]    Facility type     " " = mainline, "R" = ramp, "C" = collector-distributor
  [6:]   Sequence/suffix   varies
These flags flow into every endpoint pool and type-tier decision, making this the primary place to audit when snapping results look wrong.


Show the code
# ── Controlled-access corridors in the Wasatch Front study area ───────────
# Adding / removing a route here is the primary tuning lever for freeway coverage.
# These are the 4-character UDOT route numbers (DOT_RTNAME[0:4]).
FREEWAY_ROUTES = {
    "0015",   # Interstate 15         (primary N-S spine)
    "0067",   # Legacy Parkway        (limited-access, no ramps)
    "0080",   # Interstate 80         (E-W, SLC to Parley's Canyon)
    "0084",   # Interstate 84         (Ogden corridor)
    "0089",   # US-89                 (surface in places — watch for mis-classification)
    "0092",   # Timpanogos Highway    (SR-92, American Fork Canyon)
    "0154",   # Bangerter Highway     (semi-controlled ring road)
    "0177",   # West Davis Corridor   (new build, limited segments)
    "0201",   # SR-201                (West Valley connector)
    "0215",   # Interstate 215        (belt route, SLC)
}

rtname  = active_cl["DOT_RTNAME"].fillna("")

# ── Shared exclusion flags ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ramp/CD character check: DOT_RTNAME LIKE '%R%' or '%C%', excluding DupRoute.
_has_R_or_C = rtname.str.contains("R", na=False) | rtname.str.contains("C", na=False)
_not_duprt  = rtname != "DupRoute"
_not_ramp_cd = ~_has_R_or_C | ~_not_duprt  # True when segment is NOT a ramp/CD

# ── Class 1: Freeway Mainline ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Primary: DOT_FCLASS identifies interstate / other freeway geometry.
# Secondary: explicit UDOT route number is a controlled-access corridor.
# Tertiary: Principal Arterial with ONEWAY in ('1','2') represents a
#           physically separated directional roadway.
#           ONEWAY domain (CVDomain_OneWay): 0=Two-way, 1=One-way direction
#           of arc, 2=One-way opposite direction of arc.
# All three require exclusion of ramp/CD facility chars and DupRoute aliases.
_is_fclass_fwy = active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"].isin(["Interstate", "Other Freeway"])
_is_named_fwy  = rtname.str.slice(0, 4).isin(FREEWAY_ROUTES)
_is_dir_pa = (
    (active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"] == "Principal Arterial")
    & active_cl["ONEWAY"].isin(["1", "2"])
)

active_cl["is_freeway"] = (
    (_is_fclass_fwy | _is_named_fwy | _is_dir_pa)
    & ~_has_R_or_C
    & _not_duprt
)

# ── Class 2: Ramps and CDs ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Strictly determined by DOT_RTNAME structure: any R or C facility character,
# excluding the DupRoute administrative alias.
active_cl["is_interchange"] = _has_R_or_C & _not_duprt

# ── Class 3: Surface Streets ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Everything that is not freeway mainline or ramp/CD.
# Explicitly excludes DOT_FCLASS values that fall outside the three classes
# (already filtered in B1, but guard here for completeness).
active_cl["is_surface"] = (
    ~active_cl["is_freeway"]
    & ~active_cl["is_interchange"]
    & active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"].notna()
    & ~active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"].isin(["Interstate", "Other Freeway", "Instituitional", ""])  # note: source-data typo
)

print("Segment-level classification:")
print(f"  is_freeway     (mainline):   {active_cl['is_freeway'].sum():,}")
print(f"  is_interchange (ramp / CD):  {active_cl['is_interchange'].sum():,}")
print(f"  is_surface     (all others): {active_cl['is_surface'].sum():,}")
print(f"  unclassified   (none):       {(~active_cl['is_freeway'] & ~active_cl['is_interchange'] & ~active_cl['is_surface']).sum():,}")
print(f"  both fwy + ic  (gore segs):  {(active_cl['is_freeway'] & active_cl['is_interchange']).sum():,}")
print(f"  total active:                {len(active_cl):,}")


Segment-level classification:
  is_freeway     (mainline):   1,279
  is_interchange (ramp / CD):  1,486
  is_surface     (all others): 4,877
  unclassified   (none):       0
  both fwy + ic  (gore segs):  0
  total active:                7,642




B3 — Extract Raw Endpoints
Extract the start and end point of every active segment into a flat GeoDataFrame (two rows per segment). Carries FULLNAME, DOT_RTNAME, and the three topology flags forward for direction resolution and deduplication downstream.


Show the code
# Explode MultiLineString → LineString so get_point works correctly
_n_pre_explode = len(active_cl)
active_cl = active_cl.explode(index_parts=False).reset_index(drop=True)
print(f"After explode: {len(active_cl):,} segments (was {_n_pre_explode:,} pre-explode)")

starts = shapely.get_point(active_cl.geometry.values, 0)
ends = shapely.get_point(active_cl.geometry.values, -1)
print(f"Null starts after explode: {shapely.is_missing(starts).sum()}")  # should be 0

xs_all = np.concatenate([shapely.get_x(starts), shapely.get_x(ends)])
ys_all = np.concatenate([shapely.get_y(starts), shapely.get_y(ends)])
tile = lambda col: np.concatenate([active_cl[col].values, active_cl[col].values])

gdf_ep_raw = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "geometry": np.concatenate([starts, ends]),
        "seg_idx": tile("index")
        if "index" in active_cl.columns
        else np.concatenate([active_cl.index.values, active_cl.index.values]),
        "x_round": np.round(xs_all, 2),
        "y_round": np.round(ys_all, 2),
        "fullname": tile("FULLNAME"),
        "dot_rtname": tile("DOT_RTNAME"),
        "is_freeway": tile("is_freeway"),
        "is_interchange": tile("is_interchange"),
        "is_surface": tile("is_surface"),
        "is_start": np.concatenate([np.ones(len(active_cl), bool), np.zeros(len(active_cl), bool)]),
    },
    crs=CRS_UTM,
).reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"Raw endpoint records: {len(gdf_ep_raw):,}  (2 × {len(active_cl):,} segments)")


After explode: 7,642 segments (was 7,642 pre-explode)
Null starts after explode: 0
Raw endpoint records: 15,284  (2 × 7,642 segments)




B4 — Deduplicate by Tolerance-Based Clustering
Cluster raw endpoints by true single-linkage distance (cluster_endpoints, ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M = 1cm) rather than a rounded-coordinate grid bucket — two points 2mm apart that happen to round into different 1cm grid cells (e.g. 10.004999 → 10.00 vs 10.005001 → 10.01) are now correctly merged. Aggregate type flags with OR — a cluster is is_freeway=True if any freeway segment terminates there. The output geometry keeps the exact (unrounded) coordinate of one contributing raw endpoint rather than reconstructing a point from the rounded key, so gdf_ep_unique — and every node later snapped onto it — stays bit-exact with a real CandidateTDMRoadLinks vertex instead of sitting on a 1cm quantization grid. x_round/y_round are still carried through (first raw point) for QGIS inspection and for link_utils.resolve_snap_coords’s downstream nearest-vertex lookup, which is out of scope for this change.


Show the code
gdf_ep_raw["cluster_id"] = cluster_endpoints(
    gdf_ep_raw, tolerance_m=ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M
)

cluster_sizes = gdf_ep_raw.groupby("cluster_id").size()
print(
    f"Endpoint clusters: {len(cluster_sizes):,} clusters "
    f"from {len(gdf_ep_raw):,} raw points (tolerance={ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M}m)"
)
print(f"Cluster size distribution: {cluster_sizes.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict()}")

# Chaining-risk QA: single-linkage clustering can in principle chain several
# close-but-distinct vertices together. Flag any cluster whose raw points
# span more than 2x tolerance end-to-end (bounding-box diagonal as a cheap
# upper bound on max pairwise distance).
_span = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "cluster_id": gdf_ep_raw["cluster_id"],
        "x": gdf_ep_raw.geometry.x.values,
        "y": gdf_ep_raw.geometry.y.values,
    }
).groupby("cluster_id").agg(x_span=("x", np.ptp), y_span=("y", np.ptp))
_span["diag_m"] = np.hypot(_span["x_span"], _span["y_span"])
_chaining_risk = _span[_span["diag_m"] > 2 * ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M]
if len(_chaining_risk):
    print(f"WARNING: {len(_chaining_risk)} cluster(s) span > {2 * ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M:.2f}m — possible chaining:")
    print(_chaining_risk.sort_values("diag_m", ascending=False).head(10).to_string())
else:
    print("No chaining risk detected — all clusters within 2x tolerance.")

ep_agg = gdf_ep_raw.groupby("cluster_id", as_index=False).agg(
    x_round=("x_round", "first"),
    y_round=("y_round", "first"),
    is_freeway=("is_freeway", "any"),
    is_interchange=("is_interchange", "any"),
    is_surface=("is_surface", "any"),
    fw_route_count=(
        "dot_rtname",
        lambda s: s[gdf_ep_raw.loc[s.index, "is_freeway"]].str[:4].nunique(),
    ),
    geometry=("geometry", "first"),
)
gdf_ep_unique = gpd.GeoDataFrame(ep_agg, geometry="geometry", crs=CRS_UTM)
gdf_ep_unique["ep_uid"] = gdf_ep_unique["cluster_id"]

print(f"Unique endpoints: {len(gdf_ep_unique):,}")
print(
    f"  freeway-only   : {(gdf_ep_unique['is_freeway'] & ~gdf_ep_unique['is_interchange']).sum():,}"
)
print(
    f"  freeway + ramp : {(gdf_ep_unique['is_freeway'] & gdf_ep_unique['is_interchange']).sum():,}"
)
print(
    f"  ramp-only      : {(~gdf_ep_unique['is_freeway'] & gdf_ep_unique['is_interchange'] & ~gdf_ep_unique['is_surface']).sum():,}"
)
print(f"  surface        : {gdf_ep_unique['is_surface'].sum():,}")


Endpoint clusters: 5,195 clusters from 15,284 raw points (tolerance=0.01m)
Cluster size distribution: {1: 791, 2: 340, 3: 2620, 4: 1345, 5: 44, 6: 46, 7: 2, 8: 5, 11: 1, 12: 1}
No chaining risk detected — all clusters within 2x tolerance.

section: 5 Part C — Interchange Node Direction Enrichment
text:
5 Part C — Interchange Node Direction Enrichment
For interchange-only nodes (pass c), the directional signal is inherited one hop from adjacent freeway mainline links. This enrichment is done explicitly here (not hidden inside snap_nodes) so the lookup table is inspectable.


Show the code
# Build a flat edge list: (node_N, FT, DIRECTION) — vectorised via pd.concat
edges = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A", "FT_2027", "DIRECTION"]].rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B", "FT_2027", "DIRECTION"]].rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
edges["is_freeway_link"] = edges["FT_2027"].isin(FW_CODES)
edges["DIRECTION"]       = edges["DIRECTION"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()

CARDINAL = {"NB", "SB", "EB", "WB"}

# For each interchange-only node, collect cardinals from adjacent freeway links.
ic_only_mask = ~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node
ic_only_Ns   = set(gdf_nodes.loc[ic_only_mask, "N"])

adj_fw = (
    edges[edges["N"].isin(ic_only_Ns) & edges["is_freeway_link"] & edges["DIRECTION"].isin(CARDINAL)]
    .groupby("N")["DIRECTION"]
    .apply(lambda s: ",".join(sorted(set(s))))
)

gdf_nodes["ic_fw_directions"] = gdf_nodes["N"].map(adj_fw).fillna("")

resolved = (gdf_nodes.loc[ic_only_mask, "ic_fw_directions"] != "").sum()
total_ic  = ic_only_mask.sum()
print(f"Interchange-only nodes with freeway-neighbor direction: {resolved:,} of {total_ic:,}")
print(f"  remaining {total_ic - resolved:,} are direction-agnostic (no adjacent freeway link)")

  remaining 518 are direction-agnostic (no adjacent freeway link)

title: Node Classification
text:
6 Part D — Node Snapping
Hierarchical execution — first-call-wins. Nodes snapped in an earlier pass are skipped by subsequent passes.

D1 — Freeway and Interchange Snapping
Four passes in topology-priority order: (a) pure freeway, (a2) at-grade freeway crossings, (b) gore/gore_sf, (c) mid-ramp. All include fwy_sf in the D1 debug export so at-grade crossing snaps can be verified before running surface snapping.


Show the code
# ── Endpoint pools ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Each pool is now built from node_utils.allowed_ep_types(), which reads
# straight off _TYPE_TIER — the same table _spatial_snap uses to score
# candidates — instead of a hand-typed ep_type list. Diagnosis (2026-07-16)
# found the previous hand-typed pools had silently drifted narrower than
# _TYPE_TIER (and this section's own comments) already declared permitted:
# e.g. ("fwy", "gore"): 1 was documented as a Tier-1 fallback, but "gore"
# endpoints were never actually in the fwy pool below, so that fallback was
# dead code. Freeway/interchange node types took the brunt of it: their
# nearest real physical vertex is disproportionately a Tier-1 type one class
# over (arcpy only cuts centerlines at interchanges, not at the FT/lane
# -transition points that generate many freeway model nodes), and that
# vertex was almost always well within the search radius — median 100-150m
# vs. a 500m threshold — it just never reached the candidate pool. See
# node_utils.allowed_ep_types docstring for the full writeup. Any deviation
# from the raw tier table below is a deliberate, separately-justified
# business rule, called out inline.

# Pass (a) — fwy nodes → {fwy, gore, fwy_sf} (_TYPE_TIER tier ≤ 1 for "fwy").
#   ramp/surface are absent from _TYPE_TIER's "fwy" row entirely (not merely
#   tier>1), so they stay excluded — the divided-highway-collapse protection
#   this pool was designed for is unchanged, only the gore/fwy_sf Tier-1
#   fallback (previously dead) is now reachable.
ep_fwy_only = gdf_ep_unique[gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(allowed_ep_types("fwy"))].copy()

# Pass (a2) — fwy_sf nodes → _TYPE_TIER gives {fwy_sf, fwy, surface, gore};
#   surface is deliberately dropped here — if no fwy-class endpoint is within
#   range the node falls through to D2 (surface pass) where surface endpoints
#   are available under D2's own (more appropriate) direction logic.
ep_fwy_sf = gdf_ep_unique[
    gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(allowed_ep_types("fwy_sf") - {"surface"})
].copy()

# Pass (b) — gore + gore_sf nodes share one pool: the union of each node
#   type's _TYPE_TIER-allowed set is {fwy, fwy_sf, gore, ramp, ramp_sf}.
#   "fwy" is further restricted to multi-route hub interchanges
#   (fw_route_count >= 2) — a deliberate heuristic beyond what _TYPE_TIER
#   encodes, kept to avoid over-matching a gore node to an isolated
#   single-route fwy endpoint that merely happens to be nearby.
_gore_allowed = allowed_ep_types("gore") | allowed_ep_types("gore_sf")
ep_gore = gdf_ep_unique[
    gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(_gore_allowed)
    & ~((gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"] == "fwy") & (gdf_ep_unique["fw_route_count"] < 2))
].copy()

# Pass (c) — ramp nodes → _TYPE_TIER gives {ramp, gore, ramp_sf}.
ep_ic_only = gdf_ep_unique[gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(allowed_ep_types("ramp"))].copy()

print(f"Pass (a)  pool — fwy, gore, fwy_sf:                 {len(ep_fwy_only):,}")
print(f"Pass (a2) pool — fwy_sf, fwy, gore:                 {len(ep_fwy_sf):,}")
print(f"Pass (b)  pool — gore, fwy(hub), ramp, fwy_sf, ramp_sf: {len(ep_gore):,}")
print(f"Pass (c)  pool — ramp, gore, ramp_sf:               {len(ep_ic_only):,}")

# ── Node masks ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gore_sf (fwy+ramp+surface): included in pass (b) alongside gore nodes;
#   _TYPE_TIER gives it access to fwy_sf/ramp_sf/fwy/ramp endpoints at Tier-1
#   (folded into ep_gore's union above).
# ramp_sf (ramp+surface): skips pass (c), routes directly to D2 surface pass.
print()
print(f"Pass (a)  nodes — fwy:     {(is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node).sum():,}")
print(f"Pass (a2) nodes — fwy_sf:  {(is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node).sum():,}")
print(f"Pass (b)  nodes — gore:    {(is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node).sum():,}")
print(f"               gore_sf:    {(is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node).sum():,}")
print(f"Pass (c)  nodes — ramp:    {(~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node).sum():,}")
print(f"  ramp_sf → D2 surface:   {(~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node).sum():,}")

Pass (a2) pool — fwy_sf, fwy, gore:                 1,310
Pass (b)  pool — gore, fwy(hub), ramp, fwy_sf, ramp_sf: 2,081

# ── Pre-snap distance check ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Confirm coverage and validate distance thresholds before committing.
fwy_ic_eligible = gdf_nodes[(is_fwy_node | is_ramp_node) & ~is_transit_node]
all_fwy_ep = gdf_ep_unique[gdf_ep_unique["is_freeway"] | gdf_ep_unique["is_interchange"]]

ep_geoms   = all_fwy_ep.geometry.to_numpy()
node_geoms = fwy_ic_eligible.geometry.to_numpy()

tree_pre     = STRtree(ep_geoms)
nearest_idxs = tree_pre.nearest(node_geoms)

gdf_nodes_snapped = gdf_nodes.copy()

# _claimed: grows across passes — prevents two nodes in different passes from
# landing on the same physical endpoint.  The Gale-Shapley algorithm ensures
# uniqueness within a single pass; this set enforces it across passes whose
# endpoint pools overlap (e.g. gore endpoints appear in both ep_gore and
# ep_surface).
_claimed: frozenset = frozenset()

# Pass (a) — fwy nodes → fwy-only endpoint pool
#   Mask: fwy+ramp+surface combinations excluded — they go to passes (a2), (b), or D2.
#   Type tier: fwy ep = Tier-0 | gore/fwy_sf ep = Tier-1.
#   Direction: link_directions (freeway-priority cascade).
#   Threshold: 500m (model centroids can sit well off the physical carriageway).
gdf_nodes_snapped, _claimed = snap_nodes(
    gdf_nodes_snapped, ep_fwy_only,
    node_mask=is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node,
    max_distance_m=500, label="Freeway_Only",
    direction_col="link_directions", target_id_cols=["ep_uid", "x_round", "y_round"],
    excluded_ep_coords=_claimed,
)

# Pass (a2) — fwy_sf nodes (fwy+surface, no ramp) → fwy_sf endpoint pool
#   At-grade freeway crossings: the node touches a freeway AND a surface street.
#   Type tier: fwy_sf ep = Tier-0 | fwy/gore ep = Tier-1.
#   Surface endpoints are NOT in this pool — nodes that miss here fall to D2 where
#   surface endpoints are available as a graceful fallback.
#   Direction: link_directions (freeway component provides the cardinal signal).
#   Threshold: 500m.
gdf_nodes_snapped, _claimed = snap_nodes(
    gdf_nodes_snapped, ep_fwy_sf,
    node_mask=is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node & is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node,
    max_distance_m=500, label="Freeway_Surface",
    direction_col="link_directions", target_id_cols=["ep_uid", "x_round", "y_round"],
    excluded_ep_coords=_claimed,
)

# Pass (b) — gore + gore_sf nodes → gore endpoint pool
#   gore:    fwy+ramp, no surface — classic elevated junction.
#            Type tier: gore ep = Tier-0 | fwy/ramp/fwy_sf ep = Tier-1.
#   gore_sf: fwy+ramp+surface — at-grade interchange.
#            Type tier: gore ep = Tier-0 | fwy_sf/ramp_sf/fwy/ramp ep = Tier-1.
#            ramp_sf eps are in the pool for gore_sf; _TYPE_TIER rejects them
#            for plain gore nodes, so no false matches on elevated junctions.
#   Direction: fw_directions (freeway-only majority-vote, isolates mainline
#              direction from the ramp/CD signal at the same node).
#   Threshold: 500m.
gdf_nodes_snapped, _claimed = snap_nodes(
    gdf_nodes_snapped, ep_gore,
    node_mask=is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node & ~is_transit_node,
    max_distance_m=500, label="Freeway_Gore",
    direction_col="fw_directions", target_id_cols=["ep_uid", "x_round", "y_round"],
    excluded_ep_coords=_claimed,
)

# Pass (c) — ramp nodes (mid-ramp only, no surface) → ramp endpoint pool
#   Direction: ic_fw_directions (inherited one hop from adjacent freeway — see Part C).
#   ramp nodes have no surface links so link_directions is unreliable;
#   freeway-neighbor direction is the best available signal.
#   Threshold: 100m (mid-ramp nodes sit close to physical endpoints).
#   fwy_sf and ramp_sf nodes are intentionally excluded — both have surface links
#   and route to the surface pass (D2) where their at-grade topology is Tier-0.
gdf_nodes_snapped, _claimed = snap_nodes(
    gdf_nodes_snapped, ep_ic_only,
    node_mask=~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node & ~is_transit_node,
    max_distance_m=100, label="Interchange_Only",
    direction_col="ic_fw_directions", target_id_cols=["ep_uid", "x_round", "y_round"],
    excluded_ep_coords=_claimed,
)

D2 — Surface Snapping
All nodes with surface-class links that were not snapped in earlier passes land here. This includes: pure surface nodes, ramp_sf (ramp terminals), any fwy_sf that exceeded the pass (a2) threshold (no fwy-class endpoint within range), and any gore_sf that failed pass (b). link_directions carries the cardinal signal from all connected links.


Show the code
# Surface pool: surface, ramp_sf, fwy_sf, and gore endpoints.

CC Attachment Nodes
Centroid connector attachment nodes are the network-side endpoints of FT_2027 = 1 (centroid connector) links — the taps where zone centroids connect to the road network. Zone centroids themselves (N < 3600) are excluded; only the network attachment nodes (N ≥ 3600) are retained.
These nodes are snapped to the nearest point on the nearest physical centerline (perpendicular projection, not nearest vertex or endpoint) using a simple STRtree lookup — no direction filtering, no greedy assignment. Centroid connectors essentially never attach to freeway mainline (checked directly: 23 of several thousand real-road links touching a CC attachment node are FT 31/33/35, the mainline codes), so the undirected divided-highway collision risk that rules out this approach for road-node snapping doesn’t apply here. The result is written as a second layer in nodes_snapped.gpkg.
A CC attachment node sometimes already coincides with a real junction that the direction-aware greedy snapper above already placed — already_snapped flags those directly against this notebook’s own gdf_nodes_snapped output (the snapped column), not inferred from anything else. use_as_split = snap_resolved & ~already_snapped is the one column Stage 2/3 actually consume: reusing an already-snapped node’s independently-computed nearest- point coordinate here would plant a second, slightly different split a few cm away from the real one, producing a sliver instead of a clean cut. Unresolved nodes (> 100 m) are simply excluded — same as any other unsnapped node, no special handling.

External Station Nodes
External station nodes (EXTERNAL_ = 1 on the node table, N 3601–3629) are gateway points where the model network intentionally truncates at the edge of the modelled region — canyon passes, state lines (e.g. “I-15 to Tremonton”, “SR 190 Guardsman Pass”). Like CC attachment nodes, they get the same nearest-point-on-line treatment (not nearest-vertex) and the same already_snapped/use_as_split columns, and are written as a third nodes_snapped.gpkg layer.
The same 100 m cutoff as CC nodes is kept deliberately tight: several external nodes sit 1–13 km from any WF-county centerline (true remote boundary points where our centerline extract simply doesn’t reach), and snapping those to whatever point happens to be nearest would be a misleading match rather than a real one — better left unresolved (excluded, same as any other unsnapped node).

Re-flagging Mid-Link Attachment Nodes as Hard Boundaries
NeighborCount (Part A, top of this notebook) is computed from the FT_2027-filtered link table, so a CC node’s FT=1 spur is invisible to it. When the model inserts a CC/external attachment node strictly between two intersections — coding the through road as two separate link rows, intersection1 → node and node → intersection2 — that node sees only its two real-road neighbors and looks like an ordinary shape point: is_topo_passthrough = True. 03_transfer_attributes.qmd’s pass-through dissolve then silently walks through it, merging both halves into one chain with no split at the node’s true location and no separate attribute transfer for either half. use_as_split (computed above) is exactly the set of nodes where this applies: resolved, and not already snapped/handled elsewhere. A node already at a real junction already has is_topo_passthrough = False and needs no change.

attach_ids = set(gdf_cc_snapped.loc[gdf_cc_snapped["use_as_split"], "N"]) | \
             set(gdf_ext_snapped.loc[gdf_ext_snapped["use_as_split"], "N"])

was_mid_link_passthrough = gdf_nodes["N"].isin(attach_ids) & gdf_nodes["is_topo_passthrough"]
n_patched = int(was_mid_link_passthrough.sum())
gdf_nodes.loc[was_mid_link_passthrough, "is_topo_passthrough"] = False

gdf_nodes.to_crs(CRS_UTM).to_file(PATHS["out_node_classified"], driver="GPKG")
print(
    f"Patched is_topo_passthrough=False for {n_patched:,} mid-link CC/external "
    f"attachment node(s) (of {len(attach_ids):,} new split points total — the "
    f"rest already sat at a real junction and needed no change)."
)

2 Load Data

Model Links
Filtered the same way 01_node_classification.qmd filters when it computes NeighborCount/is_topo_passthrough: LN_2027 > 0 AND FT_2027 NOT IN (1, 37, 38, 39). Centroid connectors (FT=1) and non-physical HOV/Managed- Access links (FT=37,38,39) are excluded outright; everything else must additionally have at least one lane by 2027 to count as part of today’s (or 2027’s) connectivity graph — a link coded zero-lane in 2027 doesn’t yet exist as a driveable connection, even if a physical centerline sits near its geometry. This match matters beyond just filtering consistently: if this notebook’s dissolve graph could see an edge that 01 didn’t count, a node 01 classified pass-through (NeighborCount==2) could turn out to have a 3rd, LN=0 neighbor here — and dissolve_pseudonodes’s walk, trusting the NeighborCount==2 guarantee, would silently take the wrong edge through it. LN_2027/FT_2027 themselves are reported unchanged on matched output — this only affects whether a chain counts as connected, not what gets displayed.


Show the code
gdf_links = gpd.read_file(
    PATHS["in_network_links"],
    where="LN_2027 > 0 AND FT_2027 NOT IN (1, 37, 38, 39)",
).to_crs(CRS_UTM)

Snapped Nodes
Stage 2 guarantees every link_pieces.gpkg boundary is already a snap point, so Stage 3 needs which nodes are snapped (split points) versus not. For the “not” side, is_topo_passthrough from nodes_classified.gpkg (NeighborCount==2, regardless of FT, lane count, or link-class/designation uniformity) is safe to silently walk through and absorb into a multi-hop chain in Part A — a node with exactly two distinct neighbors has exactly one way to continue through it, full stop, no matter what changes there on the model side. An unsnapped node that fails even that (3+ neighbors — a real junction) is not pass-through: dissolve_pseudonodes’s single-preferred-edge walk has no reliable way to know which of several real branches continues the correct chain, so treating every unsnapped node as pass-through (as an earlier version of this notebook did) silently produced wrong-branch chains at those nodes. Only 2-neighbor nodes are dissolved through; any 3+-neighbor unsnapped node is left as a hard chain boundary, and pieces touching it honestly fail to match rather than getting attributed from a guessed direction.
This is deliberately broader than is_pseudo (which additionally requires uniform FT and uniform lane count, because it also gates Stage 1 snapping eligibility — a snap target needs that stricter guarantee). Stage 3 only needs the topological guarantee: real FT-transition, lane-transition, and link-class-transition nodes have no physical vertex of their own in the UGRC/UDOT centerlines (arcpy only cuts at genuine junctions), so treating them as hard chain boundaries here — while is_pseudo correctly still sends them to snapping in 01_node_classification.qmd — was silently splitting one physical piece across a model chain boundary the physical network was never actually cut at. See _plan/freeway-endpoint-pool-diagnosis.md and the node-30208 (Antelope Island Causeway) example that first surfaced this.
FixedTransit_Rail-snapped nodes are excluded from snapped_node_ids — they attach to GTFS rail infrastructure, not road centerlines, so they were never road-piece split points in Stage 2 either (02_create_link.qmd applies the same exclusion).


Show the code
gdf_nodes_snapped = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)

    gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
    & (gdf_nodes_snapped["snap_rule"] != "FixedTransit_Rail")
)
snapped_node_ids = set(gdf_nodes_snapped.loc[snapped_mask, "N"].astype(int))
n_snapped = len(snapped_node_ids)
print(f"Nodes: {len(gdf_nodes_snapped):,} total | {n_snapped:,} snapped (road, non-rail) ({n_snapped/len(gdf_nodes_snapped):.1%})")

# Snap coordinate lookup: N → (x_round, y_round)
node_coord_lookup: dict[int, tuple[float, float]] = {
    int(row["N"]): (float(row["snapped_x_round"]), float(row["snapped_y_round"]))
    for _, row in gdf_nodes_snapped[snapped_mask].iterrows()
}

# Reverse lookup: (x_round, y_round) → N — used to identify each piece's endpoints.
coord_to_node: dict[tuple[float, float], int] = {v: k for k, v in node_coord_lookup.items()}

print(f"Reverse coord→node lookup: {len(coord_to_node):,} entries")

Nodes that don’t resolve, or that coincide with a node already snapped by the main pipeline, are left out entirely (no coordinate, no split, same as any other unsnapped node).

4 Part B — Build Piece Graph
Build a networkx Graph from the physical link pieces. Each node is labelled real_junction, pseudonode, or internal based on whether it coincides with a snapped model node and whether that node is a pseudonode.

title: Transfer Model Attributes to True-Shape Links
text:
5 Part C — Assemble True-Shape Chains
For each dissolved link A→B, perform a constrained BFS through the piece graph from A’s snap coordinate to B’s snap coordinate. The BFS cannot traverse through real_junction nodes other than B — this ensures the path stays within the physical bounds of a single dissolved link.
Some dissolved links have no route between A and B that avoids every other real junction — typically an ordinary cross-street the link legitimately passes through, not a bleed into an adjacent dissolved link. When the constrained BFS fails, assemble_chain_relaxed retries with the real-junction restriction dropped, using shortest-path-by-length instead of unweighted BFS so the recovered route still follows the physically shortest path. Links recovered this way are tagged dissolved_relaxed rather than dissolved so they remain distinguishable for QA.


Show the code
print(f"Assembling {len(gdf_dissolved):,} dissolved links …")

trueshape_geometries: list = []
trueshape_methods: list[str] = []
n_unresolved = 0
n_no_path = 0
n_relaxed = 0

for i, (_, row) in enumerate(gdf_dissolved.iterrows()):
    if i > 0 and i % 2000 == 0:
        print(f"  {i:,} / {len(gdf_dissolved):,} …")

    a_n, b_n = int(row["A"]), int(row["B"])
    a_coord = node_coord_lookup.get(a_n)
    b_coord = node_coord_lookup.get(b_n)

    if a_coord is None or b_coord is None:
        n_unresolved += 1
        a_pt = node_geom_lookup.get(a_n)
        b_pt = node_geom_lookup.get(b_n)
        fallback = LineString([a_pt, b_pt]) if (a_pt and b_pt) else None
        trueshape_geometries.append(fallback)
        trueshape_methods.append("unresolved_no_snap")
        continue

    pieces = assemble_chain(piece_graph, a_coord, b_coord)
    used_relaxed = False
    if pieces is None:
        pieces = assemble_chain_relaxed(piece_graph, a_coord, b_coord)
        used_relaxed = pieces is not None

    if pieces is None:
        n_no_path += 1
        a_pt = node_geom_lookup.get(a_n)
        b_pt = node_geom_lookup.get(b_n)
        fallback = LineString([a_pt, b_pt]) if (a_pt and b_pt) else None
        trueshape_geometries.append(fallback)
        trueshape_methods.append("unresolved_no_path")
    else:
        merged = linemerge(pieces) if len(pieces) > 1 else (pieces[0] if pieces else None)
        trueshape_geometries.append(merged)
        trueshape_methods.append("dissolved_relaxed" if used_relaxed else "dissolved")
        if used_relaxed:
            n_relaxed += 1

n_dissolved = trueshape_methods.count("dissolved")
print(f"\nDissolved (true-shape):       {n_dissolved:,} ({n_dissolved/len(gdf_dissolved):.1%})")
print(f"Dissolved (relaxed fallback): {n_relaxed:,} ({n_relaxed/len(gdf_dissolved):.1%})")
print(f"Unresolved (no snap):         {n_unresolved:,}")
print(f"Unresolved (no path):         {n_no_path:,}")

title: Data Preparation
text:
3 Centerline Cleaning
Converts raw UGRC centerlines into a topology-clean CandidateTDMRoadLinks dataset that the snapping and true-shape pipeline consumes. The algorithm (dissolve → split at junctions → attribute transfer) lives in _src/centerline_utils.py; only the filter definitions belong here.

Load and Filter Raw Centerlines


Show the code
gdf_cl = gpd.read_file(
    config_filepath["out_centerlines"],
    where="DOT_RTNAME NOT IN ('DupRoute', 'Dupe') AND STATUS NOT IN ('Retired', 'Planned')",
)

# ── Wasatch Front county FIPS codes ───────────────────────────────────────
WF_COUNTIES = {"49003", "49011", "49035", "49049", "49057", "49045"}

mask_wf = gdf_cl["COUNTY_L"].isin(WF_COUNTIES) | gdf_cl["COUNTY_R"].isin(WF_COUNTIES)
gdf_wf = gdf_cl[mask_wf].copy()

# Strip leading/trailing whitespace in DOT_FCLASS (known data-quality artifact)
gdf_wf["DOT_FCLASS"] = gdf_wf["DOT_FCLASS"].str.strip()

print(f"WF centerlines: {len(gdf_wf):,} rows")


WF centerlines: 218,747 rows




Define Freeway and Surface Filters


Show the code
# ── Freeway / ramp / CD filter ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Matches arcpy: DOT_FCLASS IN ('Interstate','Other Freeway')
#                OR DOT_RTNAME LIKE '%C%'  (collector-distributor roads)
#                OR DOT_RTNAME LIKE '%R%'  (ramp roads)
FWY_FCLASS = {"Interstate", "Other Freeway"}
mask_fwy = (
    gdf_wf["DOT_FCLASS"].isin(FWY_FCLASS)
    | gdf_wf["DOT_RTNAME"].str.contains("C", na=False)
    | gdf_wf["DOT_RTNAME"].str.contains("R", na=False)
)

# ── Surface street filter ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
SURF_FCLASS = {
    "Local",
    "Major Collector",
    "Minor Arterial",
    "Minor Collector",
    "Principal Arterial",
}
mask_surf = gdf_wf["DOT_FCLASS"].isin(SURF_FCLASS)

# ── Per-vert-level splits ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# VERT_LEVEL '0' = at-grade (default); '1','2' = elevated/tunnel structures.
# Pass an empty GeoDataFrame for levels absent in this dataset; rcl_merge
# silently skips them.
_empty = gdf_wf.iloc[0:0].copy()

fwy_levels = {
    "all":  gdf_wf[mask_fwy],
    "lvl0": gdf_wf[mask_fwy & (gdf_wf["VERT_LEVEL"] == "0")],
    "lvl1": gdf_wf[mask_fwy & (gdf_wf["VERT_LEVEL"] == "1")],
    "lvl2": gdf_wf[mask_fwy & (gdf_wf["VERT_LEVEL"] == "2")],
    "lvl3": _empty,  # no VERT_LEVEL 3 in this dataset
}

surf_levels = {
    "lvl0": gdf_wf[mask_surf & (gdf_wf["VERT_LEVEL"] == "0")],
    "lvl1": gdf_wf[mask_surf & (gdf_wf["VERT_LEVEL"] == "1")],
    "lvl2": gdf_wf[mask_surf & (gdf_wf["VERT_LEVEL"] == "2")],
    "lvl3": _empty,
}

for k, v in fwy_levels.items():
    print(f"  fwy {k}: {len(v):,}")
for k, v in surf_levels.items():
    print(f"  surf {k}: {len(v):,}")

if not out_path.exists():

    print(f"Candidate links (geometry only): {len(gdf_candidate):,} rows")

    # ── Transfer attributes from original centerlines via midpoint join ────
    # OBJECTID is the persistent physical ID required for GERS lineage.
    # DOT_FCLASS, POSTTYPE, DOT_RTNAME, FULLNAME drive direction inference
    # in the snapping pipeline.
    TRANSFER_COLS = [
        "OBJECTID",

        "DOT_HWYNAM",

    print(f"Saved to: {out_path}")

section: 4 Part B — Split at Snapped Nodes
text:
4 Part B — Split at Snapped Nodes
Each candidate component is split independently at every model-node snap point and every CC attachment snap point — no merge step runs first, so components from different VERT_LEVELs are never combined. Points that project to within 0.1 mm of a component’s existing endpoint are skipped (already a boundary). After all splits, each resulting piece is bounded exclusively by: - a snapped model node position, - a snapped CC attachment node position, or - a junction/endpoint already present in CandidateTDMRoadLinks.
OBJECTID and UNIQUE_ID — the GERS lineage keys identified in the project roadmap — are copied from each parent component onto every sub-piece it produces.

cc_resolved = gdf_cc_snapped[gdf_cc_snapped["snap_resolved"]]

]
all_snap_points = snap_points_exact + cc_snap_points

print(

    f"{len(cc_snap_points):,} (CC attachment, {n_cc_unresolved:,} unresolved excluded) "

)

5 Part C — Build Pieces Layer and Export
Extract start/end endpoint coordinates for each piece (rounded to 2 dp for matching against snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round in the next stage), then export as link_pieces.gpkg with the inherited lineage-key columns.

start_coords = np.array([p.coords[0] for p in pieces])
end_coords   = np.array([p.coords[-1] for p in pieces])

gdf_pieces = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "piece_id": np.arange(len(pieces)),
        **{col: gdf_pieces_split[col].values for col in ID_COLS},

        "x_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "length_m": np.array([p.length for p in pieces]),
        "geometry": pieces,
    },
    crs=CRS_UTM,
)

PATHS["out_link_pieces"].parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

title: Create True-Shape Links
text:
3 Part A — Full Network Redissolve
CandidateTDMRoadLinks is already pre-cut at arcpy-style junction points (see 00_data_preparation.qmd’s rcl_merge), including boundaries between freeway/ramp/CD rows and surface-street rows wherever they merely touch — not just at genuine multi-way branches. To make the final true-shape split points come only from snapped model nodes, every row is re-dissolved into maximal topological chains (genuine branch points, where 3+ lines share an endpoint, still remain hard boundaries after dissolve; only incidental class-boundary splits are undone).
VERT_LEVEL isolation is preserved here, but only to prevent a specific GEOS behavior: unary_union on LineStrings doesn’t just merge lines that share an endpoint — it nodes every crossing point, inserting a new vertex (and therefore a new potential break) anywhere two lines cross in the middle, even when nothing physically connects there. Per-level isolation is what stops every elevated road from being spuriously noded against every at-grade street it merely passes over. A same-level-only merge was verified against a same-network global merge: global dissolve produced more chains (9,368) than even the raw ungrouped candidate rows (7,642) — i.e. net fragmentation, not consolidation — confirming this is a real effect at scale here, not a theoretical one. Freeway rows and surface-street rows are still dissolved together within a level — only the incidental class-boundary splits are undone; genuine branch points (3+ lines sharing an endpoint) remain hard boundaries after dissolve either way.


Show the code
vert_levels = sorted(gdf_centerlines["VERT_LEVEL"].dropna().unique())
print(f"VERT_LEVELs present: {vert_levels}")

fulldissolve_parts = []
for lvl in vert_levels:
    subset = gdf_centerlines[gdf_centerlines["VERT_LEVEL"] == lvl]
    if subset.empty:
        continue
    dissolved = dissolve_and_singlepart(subset)
    dissolved["dissolve_level"] = lvl
    print(f"  VERT_LEVEL {lvl}: {len(subset):,} rows -> {len(dissolved):,} dissolved chains")
    fulldissolve_parts.append(dissolved)

gdf_fulldissolve = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    pd.concat(fulldissolve_parts, ignore_index=True),
    geometry="geometry",
    crs=gdf_centerlines.crs,
)
print(f"\nTotal: {len(gdf_centerlines):,} candidate rows -> {len(gdf_fulldissolve):,} redissolved chains")


VERT_LEVELs present: ['0', '1', '2', '3']
  VERT_LEVEL 0: 6,940 rows -> 6,586 dissolved chains
  VERT_LEVEL 1: 669 rows -> 526 dissolved chains
  VERT_LEVEL 2: 28 rows -> 25 dissolved chains
  VERT_LEVEL 3: 5 rows -> 4 dissolved chains

Total: 7,642 candidate rows -> 7,141 redissolved chains


Sanity check: dissolve only merges touching lines into longer chains — it never adds or removes length. Total length before and after must match.


Show the code
len_before = gdf_centerlines.geometry.length.sum()
len_after = gdf_fulldissolve.geometry.length.sum()
diff_m = abs(len_before - len_after)
print(f"Total length before: {len_before:,.1f} m")
print(f"Total length after:  {len_after:,.1f} m")
print(f"Difference:          {diff_m:.3f} m")
assert diff_m < 1.0, "Redissolve changed total network length — investigate before proceeding."

text:
4 Part B — Resolve Snap Coordinates
nodes_snapped.gpkg stores snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round rounded to 2 decimal places (cm precision). Splitting and M-value operations require coordinates that exactly match a vertex stored in the centerline geometry. For each snapped node, this step finds the nearest unique centerline vertex within 5 cm and records its full-precision coordinate.
FixedTransit_Rail nodes are excluded — they snap to GTFS rail infrastructure (CRT stations, LRT midpoints), not to road centerlines, so they are never road centerline split points.


Show the code
gdf_nodes_road = gdf_nodes_snapped[

]
gdf_nodes_resolved = resolve_snap_coords(

    gdf_fulldissolve,
    tolerance=0.05,
)

n_road_snapped = gdf_nodes_road["snapped"].fillna(False).sum()
n_resolved     = gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"].sum()
n_unresolved   = n_road_snapped - n_resolved

title: Create True-Shape Links
section: 7 Part D — Build Pieces Layer, Reattach Lineage, and Export
text:
7 Part D — Build Pieces Layer, Reattach Lineage, and Export
Extract start/end endpoint coordinates for each piece (rounded to 2 dp for matching against snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round in the next stage). Since splitting now runs against the redissolved+restitched gdf_fulldissolve_restitched layer, a piece no longer maps 1:1 to a single original CandidateTDMRoadLinks OBJECTID — lineage/display attributes (TRANSFER_COLS) are reattached via the same midpoint-nearest-join approach 00_data_preparation.qmd uses to transfer attributes from raw centerlines onto CandidateTDMRoadLinks in the first place, this time from CandidateTDMRoadLinks onto each piece.


Show the code
pieces = gdf_pieces_split.geometry.tolist()
start_coords = np.array([p.coords[0] for p in pieces])
end_coords   = np.array([p.coords[-1] for p in pieces])

gdf_pieces = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "piece_id": np.arange(len(pieces)),
        "x_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "x_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "length_m": np.array([p.length for p in pieces]),
        "geometry": pieces,
    },
    crs=CRS_UTM,
)


VERT_LEVEL in the reattached output is informational only — it is the VERT_LEVEL of whichever CandidateTDMRoadLinks row lands nearest this piece’s midpoint, nothing more. VERT_LEVEL is used upstream only as a dissolve-grouping key (Part A, to keep GEOS from noding elevated roads against every at-grade crossing, and Part B2, to look up each chain’s own route identity within its own level) — it is never itself an identity check, a snap-coordinate key, a split key, or used in 03_transfer_attributes.qmd’s A/B chain matching (that gate is DOT_RTNAME + POSTTYPE, see Part B2). A piece can legitimately span a real elevation change or an ordinary street crossing with no split between — e.g. a freeway climbing onto a flyover, or HWY 186 running straight through where 1100 E crosses it — once Part B2 has restitched that specific junction. In that case the single VERT_LEVEL value carried onto the piece just reflects whichever side of the junction the midpoint happens to fall on; it is kept for future convenience (e.g. if the true-shape TDM link output later wants a VERT_LEVEL column) and should not be read as authoritative for the whole piece.
CandidateTDMRoadLinks contains a small number of standalone sub-centimetre “stub” features (max ~6 mm, confirmed by direct OBJECTID lookup) — digitizing artifacts, not anything this pipeline creates. Because split_candidate_links never cuts a component shorter than its 0.5 m _EPS, each stub passes through whole as its own piece; since both of its (near-identical) endpoints round to the same snapped-node coordinate, Stage 3 later resolves A_piece == B_piece for it — a spurious self-loop. Genuine physical loop roads (cloverleaf/collector loops that legitimately start and end at the same point) are tens of metres to several kilometres long, so a length_m < 1 m gate removes only the artifacts.


Show the code
n_before_drop = len(gdf_pieces)
degenerate_mask = (
    (gdf_pieces["x_start"] == gdf_pieces["x_end"])
    & (gdf_pieces["y_start"] == gdf_pieces["y_end"])
    & (gdf_pieces["length_m"] < 1.0)
)
n_degenerate = int(degenerate_mask.sum())
gdf_pieces = gdf_pieces[~degenerate_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
print(
    f"Dropped {n_degenerate:,} / {n_before_drop:,} degenerate zero-length pieces "
    f"(start == end, length < 1 m) — pre-existing near-duplicate-vertex stub "
    f"features already present as standalone rows in CandidateTDMRoadLinks, "
    f"not created by this pipeline. Real closed-loop roads (cloverleaf/collector "
    f"loops, tens of metres to several km long) are left untouched — the length "
    f"gate cleanly separates the two populations with a >3,000x margin."
)

gdf_pieces = transfer_attributes_by_midpoint(gdf_pieces, gdf_centerlines, TRANSFER_COLS)

n_null = gdf_pieces[TRANSFER_COLS].isna().any(axis=1).sum()
print(f"Pieces with a null transferred attribute: {n_null:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")

PATHS["out_link_pieces"].parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gdf_pieces.to_file(PATHS["out_link_pieces"], driver="GPKG")
print(f"Exported {len(gdf_pieces):,} pieces → {PATHS['out_link_pieces']}")

title: Transfer Model Attributes to True-Shape Links
text:
3 Part A — Pass-Through Chain Dissolve
Collapse chains of model links connected through pass-through nodes — the topological pass-through set (pass_through_ids = pseudo_ids - snapped_node_ids; the subtraction is defensive, these nodes are never snapped by design — see 01_node_classification.qmd’s is_topo_passthrough). A node only qualifies if it has exactly two distinct neighbors (NeighborCount==2) — that alone is the guarantee the walk needs to be safe: at a 2-neighbor node there is exactly one way to continue the chain, so dissolve_pseudonodes’s preferred-else-first-found edge choice can’t pick wrong, regardless of whether FT, lane count, or link class (freeway/ramp/ surface designation) changes there. Only a real 3+-way junction — where topology alone can’t say which branch continues the same physical road — is not pass-through here: it’s a hard chain boundary, same as a snapped node. Pieces whose real physical boundary sits at such a junction will fail to match (endpoints_only/a_only/b_only) rather than silently being attributed via a guessed branch.
Each dissolved chain spans from one snapped node (or real junction) to another; pass-through nodes along the way are absorbed regardless of any attribute change there. Every model link attribute column (besides A, B, geometry) rides along onto the dissolved output, taken from each chain’s first constituent link — this default is only provisional here; Part C replaces it with a nearest-centroid resolution for multi-constituent chains.
Unlike the old strict-pseudonode set, FT_2027/LN_2027 uniformity across a chain’s constituents is no longer guaranteed by construction — a chain can now legitimately walk through a real FT- or lane-transition node. invariant_cols=() reflects that: both columns go through the same disagreement check as everything else, and a disagreement is expected and informational (Part C’s nearest-centroid resolution is what actually decides which constituent’s attributes a given physical piece gets), not a bug.


Show the code
pass_through_ids = pseudo_ids - snapped_node_ids
print(f"Pass-through ids (is_topo_passthrough): {len(pseudo_ids):,}")
print(f"Pass-through (unsnapped) ids: {len(pass_through_ids):,}")

title: Transfer Model Attributes to True-Shape Links
text:
4 Part B — Piece-to-Chain Match
Stage 2 guarantees every link_pieces.gpkg boundary is already a snap point, so matching a piece to the dissolved chain it belongs to no longer needs any graph search — it’s a direct coordinate lookup followed by a vectorized (A,B) join:

Look up each piece’s A_piece/B_piece node id from its rounded start/end coordinate via coord_to_node (built in Part A’s node-loading section). A piece with an unsnapped endpoint (e.g. a network-boundary edge) simply gets a null on that side — that’s expected, not an error.
merge1 matches pieces drawn in the same direction as a dissolved chain (A_piece,B_piece == A,B — “forward”). merge2 matches pieces drawn in the opposite direction (B_piece,A_piece == A,B — “reverse”). Both can legitimately match the same physical piece: a typical two-way street is coded as two separate model-link rows (one per direction), each dissolving to its own A,B chain, so one physical piece produces two output rows — one per direction. A one-way road (e.g. a freeway, already digitized as a separate line per direction) matches only one side, producing one row.



Show the code
gdf_pieces["A_piece"] = pd.Series(
    list(zip(gdf_pieces["x_start"], gdf_pieces["y_start"])), index=gdf_pieces.index
).map(coord_to_node).astype("Int64")
gdf_pieces["B_piece"] = pd.Series(
    list(zip(gdf_pieces["x_end"], gdf_pieces["y_end"])), index=gdf_pieces.index
).map(coord_to_node).astype("Int64")

n_a = gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna().sum()
n_b = gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna().sum()
n_both = (gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna()).sum()
print(f"Pieces with snapped A endpoint:     {n_a:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Pieces with snapped B endpoint:     {n_b:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Pieces with both endpoints snapped: {n_both:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")

# Endpoint-status QA column — carried through to the final export regardless
# of match outcome, so an unattributed piece's geometry is still explainable.
gdf_pieces["endpoint_status"] = np.select(
    [
        gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna(),
        gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].isna(),
        gdf_pieces["A_piece"].isna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna(),
    ],
    ["both_snapped", "a_only", "b_only"],
    default="neither",
)
print(gdf_pieces["endpoint_status"].value_counts().to_string())

Show the code
# Only both-snapped pieces can possibly match an (A,B) chain — gdf_dissolved's
# A/B are never null. Filtering first (rather than merging on a nullable Int64
# key directly) sidesteps a pandas merge/factorize incompatibility with pd.NA.
both_snapped = gdf_pieces[gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna()].copy()
both_snapped["A_piece"] = both_snapped["A_piece"].astype("int64")
both_snapped["B_piece"] = both_snapped["B_piece"].astype("int64")

merge1 = both_snapped.merge(
    gdf_dissolved,
    left_on=["A_piece", "B_piece"], right_on=["A", "B"],
    how="inner", suffixes=("_piece", "_link"),
)
merge1["piece_direction"] = "forward"

merge2 = both_snapped.merge(
    gdf_dissolved,
    left_on=["B_piece", "A_piece"], right_on=["A", "B"],
    how="inner", suffixes=("_piece", "_link"),
)
merge2["piece_direction"] = "reverse"

matched = pd.concat([merge1, merge2], ignore_index=True)
n_matched_pieces = matched["piece_id"].nunique()
n_dual = matched["piece_id"].value_counts().eq(2).sum()
print(f"Matched rows: {len(matched):,}  (forward {len(merge1):,} + reverse {len(merge2):,})")
print(f"Distinct pieces matched: {n_matched_pieces:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Pieces matched in both directions (two-way streets): {n_dual:,}")
