title: Transfer Model Attributes to True-Shape Links
text:
5 Part C — Nearest-Constituent Attribute Resolution
matched can legitimately contain more than one candidate chain for the same (piece_id, piece_direction) — not only because a chain’s own constituent_ab_pairs may span multiple original hops, but because gdf_dissolved itself can contain multiple distinct chains sharing the same (A,B): self-loop branches (different loop roads that both start and end at the same real node) and genuine parallel paths (a direct link and a separate multi-hop alternate between the same two snapped nodes) both produce this. Node ids alone can’t disambiguate either case — only geometry can. A single rule handles both: explode every candidate chain’s constituent hops, join each hop to gdf_links for its attributes and geometry, measure distance from the piece’s centroid to each hop, and keep the global nearest hop per (piece_id, piece_direction) group. This simultaneously selects the correct candidate chain and the correct constituent’s attributes within it — a single-constituent, single-candidate group has exactly one hop and trivially “wins” regardless of distance.


Show the code
matched = matched.reset_index(drop=True)
matched["match_id"] = matched.index
matched["_pairs"] = matched["constituent_ab_pairs"].apply(json.loads)
matched["_piece_centroid"] = matched.geometry.centroid

exploded = matched[["match_id", "piece_id", "piece_direction", "_pairs"]].explode(
    "_pairs", ignore_index=True
)
exploded["hop_A"] = exploded["_pairs"].str[0].astype("int64")
exploded["hop_B"] = exploded["_pairs"].str[1].astype("int64")
exploded = exploded.drop(columns="_pairs")

# Safe as an exact-key join: gdf_links has zero duplicate directed (A,B) pairs.
gdf_links_idx = gdf_links.set_index(["A", "B"])
exploded = exploded.join(gdf_links_idx, on=["hop_A", "hop_B"])

centroid_lookup = matched.set_index("match_id")["_piece_centroid"]
exploded["piece_centroid"] = exploded["match_id"].map(centroid_lookup)

exploded["dist_to_centroid"] = shapely.distance(
    exploded["geometry"].to_numpy(), exploded["piece_centroid"].to_numpy()
)

print(
    f"Exploded constituent-hop candidates: {len(exploded):,} "
    f"(from {matched['match_id'].nunique():,} matched chain rows, "
    f"{matched[['piece_id','piece_direction']].drop_duplicates().shape[0]:,} distinct piece/direction groups)"
)


Exploded constituent-hop candidates: 21,098 (from 15,880 matched chain rows, 15,880 distinct piece/direction groups)




Show the code
group_sizes = exploded.groupby(["piece_id", "piece_direction"]).size()
n_ambiguous = (group_sizes > 1).sum()
print(f"(piece_id, piece_direction) groups with >1 candidate hop/chain: {n_ambiguous:,} / {len(group_sizes):,}")

best_idx = exploded.groupby(["piece_id", "piece_direction"])["dist_to_centroid"].idxmin()
resolved_attrs = exploded.loc[best_idx].copy()
print(f"Resolved rows: {len(resolved_attrs):,} (one per piece/direction group, as expected)")
assert len(resolved_attrs) == len(group_sizes)


(piece_id, piece_direction) groups with >1 candidate hop/chain: 3,261 / 15,880
Resolved rows: 15,880 (one per piece/direction group, as expected)




Show the code
# Solo-candidate groups (no ambiguity) must always keep their only hop.
solo_groups = group_sizes[group_sizes == 1].index
solo_mask = exploded.set_index(["piece_id", "piece_direction"]).index.isin(solo_groups)
solo_rows = exploded[solo_mask]
print(f"Solo-candidate groups: {len(solo_rows):,}")
print(f"  all present unchanged in resolved_attrs: {solo_rows.index.isin(best_idx).all()}")


Solo-candidate groups: 12,619
  all present unchanged in resolved_attrs: True

# Spot-check the 4 pieces identified during T7 verification as having >2 raw
# matches (self-loop / parallel-path duplicates) — each should now resolve to
# exactly one row per direction.
for pid in [1443, 336, 11353, 1264]:
    sub = resolved_attrs[resolved_attrs["piece_id"] == pid]
    raw_n = (matched["piece_id"] == pid).sum()
    hops = ", ".join(f"{d}:({a},{b})" for d, a, b in zip(sub["piece_direction"], sub["hop_A"], sub["hop_B"]))
    print(f"piece_id={pid}: {raw_n} raw candidate rows -> {len(sub)} resolved row(s) [{hops}]")

piece_id=336: 2 raw candidate rows -> 2 resolved row(s) [forward:(21652,21499), reverse:(21499,21652)]
piece_id=11353: 0 raw candidate rows -> 0 resolved row(s) []
piece_id=1264: 2 raw candidate rows -> 2 resolved row(s) [forward:(20831,20792), reverse:(20792,20831)]




Show the code
# Attach piece geometry/lineage + chain-level bookkeeping back onto the
# resolved attribute rows. The piece's own geometry (not the hop geometry,
# already spent computing dist_to_centroid) and UGRC-sourced attributes win
# any name collision with the TDM model attributes carried from gdf_links
# (e.g. both have a differently-sourced ONEWAY column) via explicit suffixes.
piece_base = gdf_pieces.set_index("piece_id")

chain_meta = matched.set_index("match_id")[["A", "B", "n_constituents", "constituent_ab_pairs"]]

gdf_matched_resolved = (
    resolved_attrs.drop(columns="geometry")
    .set_index(["piece_id", "piece_direction"])
    .join(piece_base, on="piece_id", lsuffix="_tdm", rsuffix="_ugrc")
    .join(chain_meta, on="match_id")
    .reset_index()
)
gdf_matched_resolved["trueshape_method"] = "matched"
gdf_matched_resolved = gpd.GeoDataFrame(gdf_matched_resolved, geometry="geometry", crs=CRS_UTM)

print(f"gdf_matched_resolved: {len(gdf_matched_resolved):,} rows | null geometries: {gdf_matched_resolved.geometry.isna().sum()}")

section: 6 Part D — Assemble Final Output and Export
text:
6 Part D — Assemble Final Output and Export
Every piece’s geometry is retained regardless of match outcome — pieces with no matching chain (unsnapped endpoint, or a snapped endpoint pair with no corresponding model-link chain) keep exactly one row with blank attribute columns and trueshape_method="unattributed". No synthetic/straight-line geometry is ever generated — this was the old BFS mechanism’s failure mode and the entire reason for this rewrite.


Show the code
# Drop T8's internal computation-only columns before export.
gdf_matched_final = gdf_matched_resolved.drop(
    columns=["match_id", "hop_A", "hop_B", "piece_centroid", "dist_to_centroid"]
)

matched_piece_ids = set(gdf_matched_resolved["piece_id"])
gdf_unmatched = gdf_pieces[~gdf_pieces["piece_id"].isin(matched_piece_ids)].copy()
gdf_unmatched = gdf_unmatched.rename(columns={"ONEWAY": "ONEWAY_ugrc"})
gdf_unmatched["piece_direction"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["A"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["B"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["n_constituents"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["constituent_ab_pairs"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["trueshape_method"] = "unattributed"

# Blank TDM attribute columns (ONEWAY_tdm, FT_2027, etc.) — present in the
# matched table, absent here since no chain claimed these pieces.
tdm_only_cols = [c for c in gdf_matched_final.columns if c not in gdf_unmatched.columns]
for col in tdm_only_cols:
    gdf_unmatched[col] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched = gdf_unmatched[gdf_matched_final.columns]

print(f"Matched pieces:   {len(matched_piece_ids):,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Unmatched pieces: {len(gdf_unmatched):,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")

section: 5 Part B2 — Restitch Same-Route VERT_LEVEL Transitions
text:
5 Part B2 — Restitch Same-Route VERT_LEVEL Transitions
Part A’s per-level dissolve leaves one specific kind of incidental split behind: where the same physical route continues across an elevation change (e.g. a freeway mainline climbing onto its own flyover), the two sides were dissolved in different level groups and so remain separate chains touching at a single point, even though nothing marks a real boundary there. Since bridges/flyovers have no physical model node where they rise off the ground, that point would otherwise survive all the way into the final pieces as a phantom split.
restitch_vert_level_transitions finds exactly this pattern — a coordinate shared by precisely two chain endpoints from two different levels — and merges the pair only when both sides agree on DOT_RTNAME and POSTTYPE (same route, same facility class — e.g. FWY-to-FWY, not a ramp joining the mainline) at that point, and only when the point isn’t itself a snapped model node (those must stay hard boundaries). Everything else — a different route merely crossing at a different elevation, a ramp/CD junction, a genuine 3-way branch — is left split, exactly as before.


Show the code
gdf_fulldissolve_restitched = restitch_vert_level_transitions(
    gdf_fulldissolve,
    "dissolve_level",
    gdf_centerlines,
    "VERT_LEVEL",
    identity_cols=("DOT_RTNAME", "POSTTYPE"),
    exclude_points=snap_points_exact,
    point_tolerance=0.05,
)
attrs = gdf_fulldissolve_restitched.attrs
print(f"Cross-level touch points found: {attrs['n_candidates']:,}")
print(f"  excluded (at a snapped node):     {attrs['n_excluded']:,}")
print(f"  route-identity mismatch (left split): {attrs['n_identity_mismatch']:,}")
print(f"  restitched (same route, merged):  {attrs['n_merged']:,} edges -> {attrs['n_components_merged']:,} chains")
print(f"Chains: {len(gdf_fulldissolve):,} -> {len(gdf_fulldissolve_restitched):,}")

title: Create True-Shape Links
text:
5 Part B2 — Restitch Same-Route Junctions
Part A’s dissolve only auto-merges through a true degree-2 point, so it leaves two kinds of incidental split behind, both of which strand a piece boundary with no corresponding TDM model node:

VERT_LEVEL boundaries — where the same physical route continues across an elevation change (e.g. a freeway mainline climbing onto its own flyover), the two sides were dissolved in different level groups and so remain separate chains touching at a single point. Bridges/flyovers have no physical model node where they rise off the ground.
Ordinary at-grade branch points — wherever 3+ chain-ends meet, dissolve leaves the point split even if it’s really just one through-route crossed by an unrelated street that isn’t in the TDM network at all. This turns out to be the common case: e.g. HWY 186 running through as a single continuous corridor from 900 E to 1300 E is spuriously cut where 1100 E crosses it, even though 1100 E carries no TDM link and no model node sits at that crossing.

restitch_route_through_junctions finds every coordinate shared by 2+ distinct chains and merges any pair that agrees on DOT_RTNAME and POSTTYPE (same route, same facility class) there, regardless of whether the mismatch came from a VERT_LEVEL difference or an ordinary junction — and regardless of how many other, non-matching chains also touch that same point (a crossing street stays split; only the matching through-route pair merges). Points that are themselves a snapped model node are never restitched — those must stay hard boundaries.


Show the code
gdf_fulldissolve_restitched = restitch_route_through_junctions(
    gdf_fulldissolve,
    "dissolve_level",
    gdf_centerlines,
    "VERT_LEVEL",
    identity_cols=("DOT_RTNAME", "POSTTYPE"),
    exclude_points=snap_points_exact,
    point_tolerance=0.05,
)
attrs = gdf_fulldissolve_restitched.attrs
print(f"Junction points found (2+ chains touching): {attrs['n_candidate_points']:,}")
print(f"  excluded (at a snapped node):          {attrs['n_excluded']:,}")
print(f"  candidate chain pairs considered:      {attrs['n_candidate_pairs']:,}")
print(f"  route-identity mismatch (left split):  {attrs['n_identity_mismatch']:,}")
print(f"  restitched (same route, merged):       {attrs['n_merged']:,} edges -> {attrs['n_components_merged']:,} chains")
print(f"Chains: {len(gdf_fulldissolve):,} -> {len(gdf_fulldissolve_restitched):,}")

title: Create True-Shape Links
text:
8 Part E — Centroid Connector Links
FT_2027 == 1 model links are TAZ-centroid, external-station, and transit- station connectors, not physical roadway – no centerline underlies them, so none of Parts A-D’s redissolve/split/match machinery applies. Each is already a straight two-vertex tether in the raw model; the only change here is rebuilding that tether from each node’s resolved position instead of its raw one, using the same node-coordinate cascade already computed above (main network snap -> CC/external nearest-point snap -> raw model coordinate as the final fallback). A true TAZ centroid never appears in any snapped-node table, so it always keeps its original, fixed coordinate; the network-side node moves to wherever it was actually snapped.

title: Export Final True-Shape Network
text:
3 Part A — Resolve Node Coordinates
Every node keeps its full raw attribute record; only X/Y/geometry are replaced, resolved through the same priority cascade build_centroid_connector_links already applies (raw model coordinate as the base fallback, overwritten by CC/external-station nearest-point snaps, overwritten in turn by the main greedy network snap). Listing sources lowest-priority first, highest last, means a future improved snapping pass or a brand-new node class is handled by adding one more entry to snap_sources — no other code changes.
Coordinates are resolved for every raw node here, but not every raw node survives into the final export — see Part C, which keeps only the nodes actually referenced by the final link table.


Show the code

    (
        "ext_snapped",
        gdf_ext_snapped[gdf_ext_snapped["snap_resolved"]],

        "cc_snapped",
        gdf_cc_snapped[gdf_cc_snapped["snap_resolved"]],
        "N", "x_snap", "y_snap",
    ),
    (
        "network_snapped",
        gdf_nodes_snapped[gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"].fillna(False).astype(bool)],
        "N", "snapped_x_round", "snapped_y_round",
    ),
]

coord_lookup, tier_lookup = resolve_node_coordinates(gdf_network_nodes, snap_sources)

title: Export Final True-Shape Network
section: 5 Part C — Filter Nodes to the Final Network
text:
5 Part C — Filter Nodes to the Final Network
A node belongs in the replacement file only if the final link table actually references it as an endpoint — the same referential-integrity invariant the raw MasterNet itself holds (21,923 / 21,953 raw nodes are referenced by at least one raw link). Pass-through/pseudonodes absorbed by Stage 3’s chain dissolve, and nodes touching only excluded link classes (HOV/managed-access, unmatched leftover geometry), are no longer an endpoint of anything in gdf_links_final and must not appear here — this filter is a pure referential check against the final links, not a hand-typed node-class list, so it stays correct as snapping/matching coverage improves and more nodes become genuinely used.


Show the code
used_node_ids = set(gdf_links_final["A"]) | set(gdf_links_final["B"])
print(f"Nodes referenced by final links: {len(used_node_ids):,}")

gdf_nodes_used = gdf_nodes_resolved[gdf_nodes_resolved["N"].isin(used_node_ids)].copy()

dropped_tier_counts = (
    pd.Series(tier_lookup)
    .loc[lambda s: ~s.index.isin(used_node_ids)]
    .value_counts()
)
print(f"\nUnused nodes dropped: {len(gdf_nodes_resolved) - len(gdf_nodes_used):,}")
print("Resolution tier of dropped nodes:")
print(dropped_tier_counts.to_string())
